slots.value: The default profile is Next.js + TypeScript + FSD + typia. Chapter 6 must include a client/server/shared/FSD boundary table unless a non-default stack override is explicitly documented with evidence.

Default FSD compliance requires exact layer responsibilities for app route entry, widgets/*/ui, features/*/ui, entities/*/ui, shared/ui, and components/ui, plus allowed imports, forbidden imports, public API, 600+ LOC and 1,000+ LOC split thresholds, repeated UI extraction, and exception handling rules. A non-FSD override must name the replacement layering model and evidence.

Under the default Next.js + TypeScript + FSD + typia profile, TypeScript interface/type is the source of truth for runtime schema. Every external unknown input boundary, including server action, API route handler, file upload parser, IPC, and external authentication callback, must pass a mandatory typia runtime schema validator before business logic. Create/update DTOs must use a strict typia validator that rejects excess properties, and validation failures must map to explicit error status responses. A non-TypeScript override must name the replacement runtime validation profile and evidence.
Source-of-truth tables must distinguish authoritative state from temporary cache or browser storage.
Browser-only helpers and server-safe contracts must be separated.
Coverage status must be reported as measured, proxy, or unavailable.
LoC, SLoC, token proxy, and search cost metrics require formula, scope, and source.
Validation command, result, warning, manual QA, and unverified-risk records are required.

FSD compliance must name npm run validate:fsd-structure and the automated lint/validator gate or record manual QA and unverified risk for app route entry, widgets/*/ui, features/*/ui, entities/*/ui, shared/ui, components/ui, public API, and dependency direction rules.
Artifact kinds must distinguish draft, preview, confirmed, export, public fixture, and FileAsset.
Code changes must list related docs that need synchronized updates.
